multimodal.generic_file_semantics: supports_file_input means at least one documented file/document type is accepted; inspect supports_pdf_input and provider_specific.anthropic.multimodal for exact formats.
multimodal.unknown_limit_semantics: Null exact-byte or count fields mean Anthropic does not publish that exact limit. Published MB values remain unit-tagged because Anthropic does not define MB as a byte count.

anthropic.notes: For Anthropic Claude API: current model entries accept text, image, and PDF document input and generate text output. Direct Claude API image, request, and aggregate PDF-page limits come from first-party Vision, API overview, and PDF support docs. Generic file support never implies arbitrary formats, and undocumented PDF byte/count or media-only limits remain null. Swarm fast maps to Priority Tier eligibility via service_tier=auto where Priority is documented; Swarm off maps to service_tier=standard_only. Provider Fast Mode is separate and appears as provider_specific.anthropic.serving.fast_mode with speed=fast plus the fast-mode beta header. Actual Priority assignment is capacity-dependent and returned in usage.service_tier.

image.processing: Codex client code reads and decodes PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP bytes, converts animated GIF or unsupported decoded formats to PNG, resizes non-original-detail images to the model's image limits, serializes a base64 data URL, and sends a Responses input_image item for provider-side vision processing.

client_sanity_guard.semantics: Codex source labels this 1 GiB check a high sanity guard against pathological inputs, not a protocol requirement or target upload size. It is not published as the supported provider input limit, so exact supported byte limits remain null.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: No authoritative Codex provider contract publishes a per-image byte limit, image count limit, or combined attachment byte limit. Null means unknown, not unlimited.

document.note: Codex product documentation mentions document attachments but does not publish an exact direct-input extension/MIME, representation, processing, and limit contract. Broad product attachment language is not treated as verified supported input.

pdf.note: Codex product documentation mentions PDF attachments but does not publish an exact direct-input extension/MIME, representation, processing, and limit contract. Broad product attachment language is not treated as verified supported input.

presentation.note: Codex product documentation mentions presentation attachments but does not publish an exact direct-input extension/MIME, representation, processing, and limit contract. Broad product attachment language is not treated as verified supported input.

spreadsheet.note: Codex product documentation mentions spreadsheet attachments but does not publish an exact direct-input extension/MIME, representation, processing, and limit contract. Broad product attachment language is not treated as verified supported input.

file.note: All non-image Codex attachment categories remain unknown until OpenAI publishes a complete direct-input contract. No OpenAI API-key input_file values are copied into Codex OAuth.

multimodal.attachment_semantics: Codex client/product attachment mentions are not treated as verified direct file support without exact extensions, MIME types, representation, processing semantics, and limits. Non-image categories are therefore unknown.

codex.notes: Codex OAuth is a separate provider surface from the OpenAI API. models.json supplies model-native image/text input facts; Codex prompting docs supply product attachment support. Voice dictation is client transcription, not direct audio input, and provider image-generation endpoints are separate from chat-model output modalities.

standard.request_selection: omit service_tier and use the normal accounts/fireworks/models/{model_id} model ID
standard.behavior: Default Fireworks Serverless serving path for general use.
standard.pricing: Model-specific Standard prices are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.standard when normalized.

priority.request_selection: set service_tier=priority on supported OpenAI-compatible chat completions or Anthropic-compatible messages requests
priority.behavior: Higher-reliability path during peak traffic; prioritized above Standard and less likely to be load-shed with 503s.
priority.pricing: Model-specific Priority prices are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.priority when available.

fast.request_selection: switch the request model ID to the provider-published Fast router ID for supported models
fast.behavior: High-speed serving path for latency-sensitive interactive applications; Fireworks targets 100+ generated tokens/second and says model quality remains the same.
fast.pricing: Model-specific Fast prices and router IDs are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.fast when available.

multimodal.catalog_scope: current Fireworks Serverless base models and provider-published Fast routers

image.processing: Fireworks fetches an HTTPS or mm_file asset, or decodes a MIME-prefixed base64 data URL, then preprocesses the image for the selected vision model. The public contract does not enumerate exact MIME strings for every accepted extension, so accepted_media_types remains empty/unknown rather than inferred from filename formats.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: Fireworks publishes 30 images per request, under 10 MB total for base64-encoded images, and under 5 MB plus a 1.5-second fetch timeout for each URL image. It does not define MB as exact bytes or publish exact byte limits for uploaded mm_file assets, so exact byte fields remain null.

multimodal.generic_file_semantics: The current Serverless catalog does not accept arbitrary files. mm_file:// is only an asset transport for a model-supported image.
multimodal.pdf_semantics: PDF is not a native input. Fireworks documents client-side conversion of pages to images for vision models; the removed document-inlining feature must not be advertised.
multimodal.audio_video_semantics: GLM 5.3 Flash accepts directly reachable video URLs on Serverless; audio remains unsupported there. Other documented audio/video models require dedicated deployments and remain outside this catalog.
multimodal.recommendation_semantics: swarm.labels.best_for_vision is a first-party use-case recommendation, not an alias for supports_image_input.

fireworks.notes: Fireworks multimodal capability is model- and deployment-surface-specific. Current Serverless VLM entries inherit one exact provider image contract: image_url content items accept base64 data URLs, HTTPS URLs, and mm_file uploaded-asset references; published size/count limits remain unit-tagged where Fireworks does not define exact bytes. GLM 5.3 Flash additionally accepts directly reachable video URLs in video_url content blocks and produces text; the current Serverless catalog does not natively accept PDFs, arbitrary files, or audio and does not generate media. Fireworks uses provider-native serving path names. Standard is the default base model path with no service_tier parameter. Priority is selected with service_tier=priority on supported base model paths. Fast is represented as separate provider-published router model entries such as accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p6-fast; it is not the same as Priority.

pricing.notes: Full standard Gemini API token price.

standard.notes: Default Gemini API inference tier when service_tier is omitted.

pricing.notes: Google documents Priority inference as 75–100% more than Standard.

priority.reliability: High, non-sheddable; overflow can gracefully downgrade to Standard.
priority.notes: Swarm fast maps to Google provider-native Priority inference via service_tier=priority.

multimodal.capability_semantics: modalities and capabilities are exact-model or exact-endpoint facts; swarm.labels remain recommendations and are never inferred from raw support.
multimodal.generic_file_semantics: supports_file_input means this exact model explicitly accepts PDF. It does not imply arbitrary generic files; inspect supports_pdf_input and provider_specific.google.multimodal.pdf.
multimodal.files_api_semantics: Files API and inline/URI transport carry model-supported media but do not establish model capability.

image.processing: The Gemini generateContent API decodes the image Part and processes it with native model vision. The Files API only uploads and stores bytes for later file_data reference; it does not establish that a model supports image input.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: The generateContent image guide publishes a conservative 20 MB total inline request-size limit including prompts, system instructions, and inline bytes; the broader file-input guide currently publishes a different 100 MB general payload limit. This image contract preserves the image-specific limit, does not collapse those scopes, and leaves exact bytes plus separate per-image/combined limits null because Google does not define them.

pdf.processing: Gemini uses native vision for PDF document understanding, combining natively embedded text with rendered page content so charts, diagrams, tables, and layout remain available to the model. Other document MIME types are extracted as plain text and are not part of this PDF contract.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: Google publishes 50 MB per PDF for both inline and Files API input and up to 1,000 PDF pages in one request, including requests with multiple PDFs. MB is not defined as exact bytes, and the docs do not unambiguously publish a distinct per-file page cap, so those exact fields remain null. Multiple documents plus the prompt must also fit the model context window; no exact PDF-count or combined-byte limit is published.

generate_content.inheritance_semantics: Only exact image/PDF-capable generateContent model rows inherit these contracts. Live, Interactions, embedding, prediction, and unknown API surfaces do not inherit generateContent request semantics.

multimodal.live_api_semantics: Live API is a distinct WebSocket/bidiGenerateContent serving surface. Native audio output and text/transcription events are documented separately in provider-specific output semantics.
multimodal.media_generation_semantics: Gemini image models, Imagen, Veo, Gemini Omni, Lyria, and TTS entries publish their own output modalities; media output is never inferred from a neighboring family.

image_generation_settings.unknown_semantics: Every Google image-output row has an explicit settings profile. status=unknown means clients must not advertise synthesized nil/default controls.
image_generation_settings.managed_tool_semantics: provider_specific.google.image_generation.managed_image_tool records whether Swarm's current managed image tool accepts the exact model ID; supported_values remain model-specific.

video_generation_settings.unknown_semantics: Every Google video-output row has an explicit settings profile. Fixed output facts, unsupported selectors, and unknown selectable ranges remain distinct.
video_generation_settings.conditional_semantics: settings.variants and features.conditions preserve mode-, resolution-, feature-, and region-specific constraints; clients must not flatten them into universal enums.

multimodal.unknown_alias_semantics: Hot-swapped latest aliases or stale exact versions without a current exact first-party modality table remain explicitly unknown.

google.notes: Google multimodal metadata uses first-party Gemini Developer API model pages and exact API-surface guides, not Vertex-only metadata or adjacent-version assumptions. Image/PDF-capable generateContent rows now inherit exact provider request representations, MIME/transport, native processing, and published-limit semantics; incompatible API surfaces do not. Gemini thinking controls remain model-family dependent and separate from recommendations. Google serving exposes Standard and Priority only in this catalog pass; Flex and Batch are intentionally not exposed as Swarm serving tiers.

standard.notes: Default OpenAI API serving tier when Priority/Flex is not requested.

priority.notes: Swarm fast maps to OpenAI provider-native Priority processing via service_tier=priority. This is OpenAI API metadata only, not Codex OAuth.

flex.notes: OpenAI Flex processing for latency-tolerant synchronous API requests via service_tier=flex.

batch.notes: OpenAI Batch API pricing; this is an asynchronous API surface, not a service_tier value on synchronous requests.

multimodal.generic_file_semantics: supports_file_input means at least one documented Responses API input_file category is accepted; inspect supports_pdf_input and provider_specific.openai.multimodal for exact handling.

image.processing: The provider decodes and processes the image as vision input. GIF support is limited to non-animated GIF input.

limits.exact_byte_semantics: OpenAI publishes a 512 MB total request payload limit but no separate per-image byte limit and does not define MB as an exact byte count. Exact byte fields remain null rather than importing the ChatGPT product's 20 MB image limit or guessing a conversion.

pdf.processing: OpenAI extracts text and renders every PDF page as an image; vision-capable models receive both extracted text and page images, while text-only models receive extracted text only.

presentation.processing: OpenAI extracts text from the presentation. Embedded images and charts are not added to model context; convert the file to PDF when visual fidelity is required.

rich_document.processing: OpenAI extracts text from the document. Embedded images and charts are not added to model context; convert the file to PDF when visual fidelity is required.

spreadsheet.processing: OpenAI applies spreadsheet augmentation: it parses up to the first 1,000 rows per sheet and adds generated summary and header metadata instead of passing entire sheets to the model.

text_and_code.processing: OpenAI extracts textual content. This category is provider-processed input_file context, not an arbitrary binary-file contract.

limits.exact_byte_and_count_semantics: OpenAI publishes under 50 MB per file and 50 MB combined across files, but does not define MB as an exact byte count, a maximum file count, or a maximum PDF page count. Exact fields remain null rather than guessed.

openai.notes: For OpenAI API only: model pages define native modalities, while Responses API input_file processing supplies file/PDF context. Image generation is a separate tool output, not native output from these code-LLM entries. Swarm fast maps to provider service_tier=priority. Codex OAuth remains separate.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter's public Models API exposes base model pricing but does not expose service-tier-specific pricing.

default.notes: Default OpenRouter routing when service_tier is omitted. OpenRouter may normalize upstream base-tier labels, such as Google standard, to default in responses.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents priority as faster and higher cost, but does not expose per-model priority availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

priority.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=priority, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents flex as lower cost and higher latency, but does not expose per-model flex availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

flex.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=flex, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

service_tiers.notes: OpenRouter service_tier is documented as a router-level request parameter with priority/flex values, but /api/v1/models does not list service_tier in supported_parameters and does not publish per-model tier availability or tier pricing. Swarm therefore records this metadata as disabled/unmapped and does not add service_tier to OpenRouter model supported_parameters.

multimodal.catalog_scope: The complete OpenRouter catalog is requested with output_modalities=all; the endpoint otherwise defaults to text output and omits dedicated media, embedding, rerank, speech, transcription, and video rows.
multimodal.capability_semantics: Each row's architecture.input_modalities and architecture.output_modalities are OpenRouter router-advertised compatibility facts. They are not inherited upstream claims and do not guarantee identical native behavior, formats, or limits across every routed provider endpoint.
multimodal.routing_semantics: OpenRouter may choose among providers. Exact route availability and media handling can vary by provider; model rows therefore describe the router contract, while provider_specific.openrouter.multimodal records that variation explicitly.
multimodal.unknown_semantics: Missing, empty, or newly unrecognized API modality values normalize to unknown and produce null capability booleans rather than false certainty.
multimodal.file_pdf_semantics: OpenRouter accepts PDF file content for every model. If the selected route supports files natively it may pass the PDF through; otherwise OpenRouter parses it and forwards parsed results. supports_pdf_input and supports_file_input describe this router contract, while provider_specific.openrouter.multimodal.transport.pdf.model_native_when_file_advertised preserves the native-versus-processed distinction.

image.processing: OpenRouter accepts the unified image_url contract and routes the request to an image-capable upstream provider. Exact native preprocessing can vary by selected provider route; the router contract does not claim identical upstream handling.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: OpenRouter documents that image-count limits vary by provider and model and publishes no router-wide exact image byte or combined attachment limit. These fields remain null/unknown rather than inheriting an upstream provider's limits.

pdf.processing: When the selected route supports native file input, OpenRouter can pass the PDF to that provider. Otherwise OpenRouter parses it and forwards extracted text and, when supported, extracted images. The default prefers native processing and otherwise uses the router parser.

parser_engines.native: Passes the PDF to a route with native file support and produces no parsed annotation.
parser_engines.mistral_ocr: Router-side OCR for scanned or image-bearing PDFs; extracted text is preserved, with at most eight extracted images per PDF/request forwarded downstream.
parser_engines.cloudflare_ai: Router-side conversion of the PDF to Markdown.

limits.exact_limit_semantics: The eight-image values constrain images extracted by the Mistral OCR parser; they are not PDF page, file-count, or input-image limits. OpenRouter publishes no router-wide PDF byte, file-count, page-count, or combined attachment byte limit, so those fields remain null/unknown.

multimodal.transport_semantics: Chat content types and dedicated media/embedding/rerank endpoints are transport surfaces, not evidence that an arbitrary model row supports that modality. Inspect the exact row's router-advertised modalities.
multimodal.recommendation_semantics: Raw capability metadata never sets Swarm best-for labels or onboarding recommendations.

openrouter.notes: OpenRouter capability fields describe the router's live catalog, not guaranteed identical upstream-provider behavior. The provider contract now records exact router-wide image MIME/transport semantics and universal PDF representation/processing semantics while leaving route-varying or unpublished byte/count/page limits null. The complete catalog includes every output class, PDF router processing stays separate from native file support, recommendation labels remain independent, and fast/flex remain disabled because per-model tier support and pricing are unverified.

batch.capacity_behavior: Separate asynchronous workflow outside normal synchronous capacity planning.

serving.notes: Anthropic serving tiers mapped for Swarm: off=Standard via service_tier=standard_only, fast=Priority via service_tier=auto where Priority is documented, and batch=Batch API. anthropic.note: Models API supplies identity, release timestamp, token limits, and machine-readable capabilities. image.limit_scope: Direct Claude API. Anthropic publishes 10 MB per base64-encoded image but does not define MB as a byte count, so the exact bytes field remains null. URL and Files API sources are not assigned an undocumented per-image byte limit.

file.note: Generic file input means at least one documented file type is accepted; it does not imply arbitrary binary file support.

pdf.limit_scope: Anthropic publishes aggregate request and page limits, not a separate per-PDF byte cap or PDF-count cap.

request.limit_scope: Direct Claude API Messages request payload, including text, images, PDFs, and all other request content. Anthropic publishes 32 MB without defining MB as a byte count, so the exact bytes field remains null. Anthropic does not publish a separate media-only combined byte cap.

multimodal.notes: Current Claude models accept text, image, and PDF document input and generate text output. Direct Claude API limits are recorded exactly where Anthropic documents them. Null per-PDF and media-only byte/count fields mean Anthropic does not publish a separate exact limit, not that the input is unlimited.

batch.notes: Batch is a separate Anthropic API surface, not a service_tier value on synchronous Messages requests.

serving.notes: Anthropic serving tiers mapped for Swarm: off=Standard via service_tier=standard_only, fast=Priority via service_tier=auto where Priority is documented, and batch=Batch API. Anthropic provider Fast Mode is represented separately as serving.fast_mode with speed=fast and is not the same as Priority Tier. Priority assignment is capacity-dependent and reported in response usage.service_tier.

anthropic.note: Models API supplies identity, release timestamp, token limits, and machine-readable capabilities. Anthropic service-tier, provider Fast Mode, and thinking-control metadata is documented in provider_specific.anthropic.serving/thinking fields; model aliases, cloud provider IDs, knowledge cutoffs, and deprecation dates require follow-up official-docs enrichment.

image.limit_scope: Direct Claude API. Anthropic publishes 10 MB per base64-encoded image but does not define MB as a byte count, so the exact bytes field remains null. URL and Files API sources are not assigned an undocumented per-image byte limit.

file.note: Generic file input means at least one documented file type is accepted; it does not imply arbitrary binary file support.

pdf.limit_scope: Anthropic publishes aggregate request and page limits, not a separate per-PDF byte cap or PDF-count cap.

request.limit_scope: Direct Claude API Messages request payload, including text, images, PDFs, and all other request content. Anthropic publishes 32 MB without defining MB as a byte count, so the exact bytes field remains null. Anthropic does not publish a separate media-only combined byte cap.

multimodal.notes: Current Claude models accept text, image, and PDF document input and generate text output. Direct Claude API limits are recorded exactly where Anthropic documents them. Null per-PDF and media-only byte/count fields mean Anthropic does not publish a separate exact limit, not that the input is unlimited.

swarm.notes: Anthropic entry hydrated from the authenticated first-party Models API. Claude API service-tier metadata is mapped for Swarm off/fast/batch where documented; provider Fast Mode is represented separately as serving.fast_mode; and Claude thinking controls are mapped from first-party adaptive/effort/extended-thinking docs. Pricing, alias, deprecation, and cloud-provider mapping enrichment is pending.

models.description:
Kimi K3 is Kimi’s most capable flagship model to date, with 2.8 trillion parameters. It is built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), with native visual understanding and a 1M-token context window. It is the world’s first open-source model in the 3-trillion-parameter class, with comparable performance to leading close-source models. It is available on both Fast and Priority serverless tiers, as well as with US-only serverless endpoints for workloads in regulated industries. All Fireworks inference comes with zero data retention enabled by default.

→ Use Priority for max reliability during congestion; priced at +25% from standard rates.

→ Use Fast for max speed or latency-sensitive workloads; priced at +50% from standard. To use Fast, switch model ID to the Fast variant: accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-fast

→ Use the US-only endpoint for necessary workloads; priced at +10% from standard rates. To do so, switch to model ID: accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-us

models.description: Muse Glimmer 30B is a dense causal language model distilled from Muse Spark and purpose-built for autonomous agentic work. It combines multi-step reasoning, reliable schema-based tool calling, and failure recovery with multimodal understanding via a ~1.8B ViT-G/14 perception encoder, supporting interleaved text and image input, a 131K+ context window, and selectable reasoning strength (low through xhigh). Trained on data from over 100 languages, Muse Glimmer performs strongly for its size class on agentic benchmarks including MCP Atlas, DeepSearch QA, Gaia2 and SWE-Bench Pro, and is released under Apache 2.0.

models.description: Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 is a frontier-scale large language model (LLM) trained by NVIDIA, designed to deliver strong agentic, reasoning, and conversational capabilities. It is optimized for the most demanding workloads, including complex multi-step agents, long-context analysis, and high-accuracy reasoning over code, math, and science. The model employs a hybrid Latent Mixture-of-Experts (LatentMoE) architecture, utilizing interleaved Mamba-2 and MoE layers, along with select Attention layers. Like the Super model, the Ultra model incorporates Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) layers for faster text generation and improved quality, and it is trained using an NVFP4 pre-training recipe to maximize compute efficiency. The model has 55B active parameters and 550B parameters in total.

Swarm therefore records this metadata as disabled/unmapped and does not add service_tier to OpenRouter model supported_parameters.

reasoning.note: Swarm maps only the exact effort values in this model's live OpenRouter reasoning object. A non-mandatory model also exposes off through reasoning.enabled=false. Gateway-wide reasoning support is not used to invent model-specific effort levels.

openrouter.note: OpenRouter capability fields describe the router contract and its live catalog, not guaranteed identical native behavior on every upstream route. PDF processing works at the router for every model, while architecture file modality marks native/provider file handling. Service tiers remain unmapped and recommendation labels remain independent of capabilities.

pdf.note: This row does not advertise native file capability, so OpenRouter parses the PDF and forwards parsed results.

pdf.capability_note: supports_pdf_input is a router processing contract. It is deliberately separate from native file capability and does not imply arbitrary file formats.

multimodal.recommendation_semantics: swarm.labels and onboarding recommendations are Swarm-owned recommendations; they are never inferred from router-advertised capability modalities.
